idiom_name: dispatcher Map keyed by the discriminator (or an ordered predicate list) with an explicit fallback
implementation_notes: JavaScript has no runtime types, so the router is explicit data: a Map (or object literal) from the message's discriminator to its handler, with one lookup replacing the switch/if chain, plus an array of [predicate, handler] rows evaluated in order when rules depend on values rather than a single key. Node's EventEmitter is the same shape with the event name as the key (emitter.on(kind, handler)), while broker bindings (amqplib, KafkaJS, BullMQ) route on the routing key or queue name chosen by the producer - so a decision that needs the decoded body stays in this in-process dispatcher. Build the table once at startup and treat it as immutable, which gives the rules one definition and one place to test.
pitfalls: A missing key returns undefined, so invoking the handler without a fallback throws a TypeError far from the routing decision - the fallback belongs in the lookup, not in an outer try/catch.
msg.kind is untrusted JSON: without validation (zod/ajv) an absent or unknown discriminator routes to the fallback or crashes, so validate the discriminant before dispatch.
Mutating the routes Map at runtime re-creates Dynamic Router semantics by accident and races with in-flight messages; build it once and freeze it.
